The defendants No.1-5 contested the suit by filing written statements denying the material allegations made in the plaint and stating, inter alia, that the Zaminder by Patta being No.105 settled the suit land in favour of the defendants predecessor Anu Mia. That thereafter more 10.17 acres of land was settled with Sultan Ahmed and others Vide Patta No.68 of 1976. The M. R. R. Khatian and B. S. Khatian was prepared in their names. The other lands were settled with Sirajul Mostafa and others by Dakhila. The M.R.R. Khatian No.137 was recorded in their names and that the settlement holders have been in possession of 3.82 acres of land in Plot No.106. Hirod Chandra had no subsisting interest in the land of Plot No.106. Thereafter the rent receiving interest was acquired by Zaminder who had no interest and the land was vested to the Government and area of 1.39 acres of land of the defendant was wrongly recorded in khas khatian No. l. That the B. S. Khatian was correctly recorded in respect of 2.51 acres of land and that the Government had no title and possession in the land of Plot No.106 and the Government was not entitled to settle any land from that plot. The Government was not entitled to settle any land from that plot and with these averments the defendants claimed for dismissal of the suit. 

 7. The learned Counsel Mr. Golam Rabbani with Mr. Ruhul Bari Sharif appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent-petitioners submits that the learned Joint District, Cox's Bazar is absolutely wrong and erroneous in allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Cox's Bazar. The learned Counsel next submits that the trial court after scrutinizing and weighing the evidence on record and also perusing the papers and documents passed the judgment and decree which was absolutely correct and proper. The learned trial court rightly observed in his judgment that the Pattas did not specified the suit land as such the suit land is vague and unspecified. The learned Counsel further submits that the defendants ought to have been filed a case for correction of M.R.R.  record if at all the suit land was wrongly recorded in M.R.R. Khatian but the defendant did not take any steps to correct the M. R. R. Khatian. The learned Counsel also submits that the appellate court should reverse the finding of the trial court with reference to the evidence on record but in the instant suit the learned Joint District Judge without referring the evidence on record reverse the finding of the trial court which is absolutely wrong and illegal and as such liable to be interfered by this court. The learned Counsel finally submits that the lower appellate court without taking into consideration of the legal provision of Order-XLI, Rule-31 came to wrong and erroneous finding and acted illegally in reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial court which is liable to be set aside and interfered by this court and hence the rule should be made absolute. 

 8. On the other hand the learned Counsel Mr. Md. Alamgir Kitbir appearing on behalf of the defendant-appellant-opposite parties submits that the finding of facts whether concurrent or not arrived at by the lower appellate court is final unless it is manifestly perverse. Next he submits that the lower appellate court was absolutely right and justified in arriving at its finding and decision in reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial court because there is no misreading and non-consideration of the evidence on record which calls for no interference by this court in revisional jurisdiction. The learned Counsel further submits that the defendant after obtaining Patta from Zaminder has been owning and possessing the suit land since a long without any interruption from any quarter. He also submits that the argument advance by the learned Counsel for the petitioner that the Patta was unspecified was not correct. The Zaminder by these Pattas distributed all his khas land to different tenant and no khas land was left with the possession of the Zaminder. The learned Counsel further submits that the learned appellate court rightly observed in his judgment that if the Government would acquire the khas land of Zaminder in that case the lessee plaintiff-petitioners would produce compensation assessment roll to prove their bonafide but in the present case the plaintiff-petitioner could not produce any compensation assessment roll to show that Government acquire the suit land from the Zaminder by giving compensation. The learned Counsel to refute the argument of the lawyer of the other side submitted that with regard to preparation of record of right and correct of M.R.R. Khatian he submits that under Section 144 A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act new record will prevail upon the old record.
